name: Vettalon
description: Vettalon is a command-line tool that checks your own code for security vulnerabilities, using open-source scanners plus AI models from several vendors, where a model from a different vendor tries to refute each finding.
description_good_justification: The README opens with one sentence on what the tool does: it finds security vulnerabilities in your own code, with AI models from several vendors and a cross-vendor check of each finding. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/README.md
interact_justification: The README Install section explains how to get the software (https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/README.md#install). Bug reports and feature requests go to GitHub Issues, and CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to contribute (https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md describes the process: branch from main, open a pull request against main, CI must pass. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md lists the requirements: cargo fmt, clippy with -D warnings, passing tests, Conventional Commits, docs and CHANGELOG updated in the same PR. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
floss_license_osi_justification: Apache-2.0 is approved by the OSI.
license_location_justification: The license is in the top-level LICENSE file. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/LICENSE
documentation_basics_justification: The README covers install (npm or build from source), quick start, usage examples, and a Security boundaries section on safe use. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/README.md
documentation_interface_justification: The README Usage section documents the CLI commands and options, and `vettalon --help` prints every option. The JSON report format is defined in https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/crates/vettalon/src/audit/schema.rs and SARIF output follows SARIF 2.1.0.
sites_https_justification: The website https://vettalon.dudustudio.monster, the GitHub repository and the GitHub release downloads all use HTTPS. The website redirects HTTP to HTTPS.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues, pull requests and Discussions are public, searchable, linkable by URL and need no proprietary client. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/issues and https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/discussions
english_justification: README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and SECURITY.md are in English, and the project accepts issues and comments in English. A Traditional Chinese README is provided as well.
maintained_justification: Releases 0.1.0, 0.1.1 and 0.2.0 shipped between 2026-10-15 and 2026-10-17, and main was last updated on 2026-10-18. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/commits/main
repo_track_justification: Git records each change with its author and date.
repo_interim_justification: Work happens in commits and pull requests between releases; for example PR #6 was merged after the v0.2.0 release. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/pull/6
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique version number (0.1.0, 0.1.1, 0.2.0). https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/releases
version_semver_justification: Versions follow SemVer, as stated at the top of the changelog. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
version_tags_justification: Each release has a Git tag (v0.1.0, v0.1.1, v0.2.0). https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/tags
release_notes_justification: CHANGELOG.md has a human-readable section per release (Added, Changed, Fixed, Security), following Keep a Changelog. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No vulnerability has been reported against Vettalon itself. Releases that fix known vulnerabilities in dependencies list their IDs under a Security heading, for example 0.2.1 lists RUSTSEC-2026-0346 to 0349. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
report_process_justification: Bugs are reported through GitHub Issues, with an issue form that asks for version, install method and OS. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/issues
report_responses_justification: The repository became public on 2026-10-13 and has not yet received a bug report from anyone other than the maintainer, so there are no unanswered reports. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/issues?q=is%3Aissue
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement requests from outside the maintainer have been filed yet. The three open issues are starter tasks opened by the maintainer. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/issues
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues keeps a public, searchable archive of reports and replies. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md describes how to report a vulnerability, and the website publishes the same contacts in security.txt. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/SECURITY.md and https://vettalon.dudustudio.monster/.well-known/security.txt
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled; reports go through https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/security/advisories/new as SECURITY.md explains. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received in the last 6 months. SECURITY.md commits to a first reply within 7 days.
build_justification: The project builds with Cargo (`cargo build`), as documented in the README Development section and run in CI. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/README.md#development
build_common_tools_justification: Cargo, the standard Rust build tool.
build_floss_tools_justification: The Rust toolchain and Cargo are FLOSS. No proprietary tools are needed to build.
test_justification: The Rust test suite (`cargo test`) is part of this Apache-2.0 repository. How to run it is documented in CONTRIBUTING.md and the README, and CI runs it on Linux and macOS. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_invocation_justification: Tests run with `cargo test`, the standard Rust command.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs fmt, clippy and tests on every push to main and on every pull request. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/actions/workflows/ci.yml
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires automated tests with new functionality and bug fixes in the same pull request, and the pull request template has a checkbox for it. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
tests_are_added_justification: Recent major changes added tests with the feature, for example the supply-chain hunt commit (https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/commit/4b7e29aa33aebfdcb4597da4c1012e86169995b1) and the 0.2.0 release commit (https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/commit/e3493f620487d23dbbd6a13021c216f415974585).
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md and the pull request template ask for automated tests with every new feature or bug fix. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md
warnings_justification: CI runs `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, which also reports rustc warnings. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
warnings_fixed_justification: Clippy runs with -D warnings, so any warning fails CI. The latest CI runs on main pass.
warnings_strict_justification: Warnings are treated as errors (-D warnings) for all targets, including tests.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer applies secure design in the code: fail-closed security gates (CONTRIBUTING.md), least privilege for model CLIs and PoC containers, path canonicalization, and secret masking, described in https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/README.md#security-boundaries
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer knows the common error classes for this kind of tool (path traversal, archive extraction attacks, command injection, prompt injection, secret leakage) and the code has mitigations for them, described in https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/README.md#security-boundaries and https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/SECURITY.md
crypto_published_justification: Vettalon uses only published algorithms: SHA-256 (sha2 crate) for hashes and TLS through rustls for network requests.
crypto_call_justification: Cryptography comes from dedicated libraries (sha2, rustls via reqwest). The project does not implement its own.
crypto_floss_justification: All cryptographic libraries used (sha2, rustls) are FLOSS.
crypto_keylength_justification: Vettalon does not choose key lengths itself. TLS uses rustls defaults, which reject RSA keys under 2048 bits and only offer modern TLS 1.2 and 1.3 suites.
crypto_working_justification: No broken algorithms are used. Hashing uses SHA-256 and TLS uses rustls, which does not support MD5, RC4 or DES suites.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: Default mechanisms use SHA-256 and rustls TLS 1.2/1.3; SHA-1 and CBC-mode SSH are not used.
crypto_pfs_justification: TLS connections use rustls, which only supports ECDHE key exchange, so sessions have forward secrecy.
crypto_password_storage_justification: Vettalon does not authenticate users and stores no user passwords.
crypto_random_justification: Vettalon does not generate cryptographic keys itself. TLS key and nonce generation is done by rustls with a cryptographically secure generator.
delivery_mitm_justification: Releases are downloaded over HTTPS from GitHub Releases and npm. Each archive also has a cosign keyless signature and GitHub build provenance; see https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/docs/TRUST.md
delivery_unsigned_justification: SHA-256 files are served over HTTPS next to the archives, and each archive also has a cosign signature that can be checked with the steps in https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/docs/TRUST.md
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no publicly known medium or higher vulnerabilities in Vettalon older than 60 days. Dependency advisories for zip and rustls were published 2026-10-09 to 2026-10-14 and are tracked for update.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Security problems found so far were fixed in the next release, for example the 0.2.0 fix that stops secret files from being sent to models. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
no_leaked_credentials_justification: The repository holds only fake test values, marked with gitleaks:allow or listed in .gitleaksignore. A gitleaks scan of the full history found no leaks, and GitHub secret scanning with push protection is on.
static_analysis_justification: Clippy, a static analysis tool separate from the compiler with several hundred lint checks, runs with -D warnings on every push and pull request, and CI passed on each release commit before tagging. https://github.com/zhixuli0406/vettalon/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: Clippy looks for general defects. No vulnerability-focused static analyzer (for example Semgrep or CodeQL) runs on this repository yet.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Clippy findings block CI and none are open. No medium or higher vulnerability has been found by static analysis.
static_analysis_often_justification: Clippy runs on every push to main and every pull request.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No fuzzer or other dynamic analysis tool is run against Vettalon itself before releases.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: Vettalon is written in Rust, a memory-safe language. The only C file in the repository is a test fixture, not part of the shipped program.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Tests run in the Cargo debug profile, which enables debug_assert! checks and integer overflow checks.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis is run yet, so no vulnerabilities have been found that way.
